text:
The Bruins stopped a three-game skid by beating Detroit on Wednesday, the night after a 3-0 home loss to Los Angeles that had Marco Sturm reshuffling his forward lines in the third period (as 98.5 The Sports Hub's Ty Anderson noted). At 14-7-1 with 29 points, Boston is comfortably in a playoff spot. The question is how much of that is the team and how much is the crease.

Our numbers say a lot of it is the crease. The Bruins have 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 53% at five on five, which is solid but not dominant. They've allowed 10.77 fewer goals than those chances usually produce, and by our count that's worth about 4.1 extra points. Michael DiPietro has been a big part of it lately, .926 and 3.5 goals saved above expected over his last five starts.

The best thing on the roster is the Hampus Lindholm and Charlie McAvoy pair: 65% of the expected goals in 242 minutes together. Up front, David Pastrnak, Pavel Zacha and JJ Peterka have outscored teams 9-5, even as Daily Faceoff asks what Boston should do with Zacha. Rookie James Hagens is out a few weeks, per Sturm. Our playoff odds sit at 79%. Watch whether the five-on-five play rises to meet the goaltending before the goaltending comes back to earth.
headline: The Bruins are winning on goaltending
